abstract: Blood pressure is a critical indicator that should be checked often to avoid hypertension symptoms, suggesting cardiac problems, strokes, and sudden death. Blood pressure should be measured as precisely as possible to provide proper diagnosis and treatment. The manual auscultation method is the gold standard for noninvasive blood pressure monitoring. However, this approach is still regarded as very subjective. Several automation approaches are being developed, including the oscillometric method, ultrasonography, PPG, and automated auscultation. Automated auscultation has been grown since around 2000, but this method is still not as developed as automatic oscillometric. Because the auscultation method is still the primary reference standard and automated methods might minimize blood pressure reading mistakes, this article will explicitly examine the automatic auscultation for blood pressure measurement, especially equipment and signal processing. Further development of automated auscultation will focus on using advanced technology, such as wireless devices and the Internet of Things (IoT).

articleTitle: Reinforcement Learning Based Energy Storage Units Scheduling Considering Point of Common Coupling Constraint
publicationTitle: 2021 3rd International Symposium on Material and Electrical Engineering Conference (ISMEE)
abstract: In this paper, agent-aggregators cooperation has been introduced in Smart Microgrid (SMG) consisting of household users, Photo Voltaic array (PV), and Local Energy Storage System (LESS). The SMG has Energy Management System called agent deal with two aggregators to purchase the energy for the consumers. Each aggregator supplying a limited level of energy from different energy resource, where one aggregator depend on Community Energy storage System to provide power in one direction to the users and the other aggregator supplying power from the utility grid. The job of the agent is to decide the optimum amount of purchasing power from the aggregators at the lowest cost to supply the users and to charge the LESS taking into account the constraints of supplying limitations for both CESS and utility grid at Point of Common Coupling. Each aggregator supplies a limited level of energy from different energy resource, where one aggregator depend on the Community Energy storage System (CESS) to provide power in one direction to the users and the other aggregator supplying power from the utility grid. The job of the agent is to decide the optimum amount of purchasing power from the aggregators at the lowest cost to provide the users and to charge the LESS taking into account the constraints of providing limitations for both CESS and utility grid at Point of Common Coupling (PCC).A model-free Reinforcement Learning (RL) method is used as an essential strategy to achieve the proposed task using Deep Q-Network (DQN). The simulation result is done and the results are verified using Improved Particular Swarm (IPSO) as a benchmark method. The obtained results show the efficiency and effectiveness of the method used

articleTitle: Technology and Social Communication: Challenge for Gojek Female Riders during the Covid-19 pandemic
publicationTitle: 2021 3rd International Symposium on Material and Electrical Engineering Conference (ISMEE)
abstract: This research aims to know the Gojek female riders survive during the pandemic by optimize their ability of social communication through technology. A qualitative approach and case study method are used in this research. Media Richness Theory has become a tool to explore and to analyse. The result has shown that technology has helped the Gojek female riders by providing channels, tools, and opportunity to improve their life. In parallel, the limitation and complexity of technology has also developed their communication skill to keep their job during the pandemic Covid19. It is an obligation that come unpredictably however must be handled. No training no brief information nothing provided but in the end sharpening their social communication skills within their interaction using the application has become the best solution.

articleTitle: A Microfluidic Impedance Flow Detection Platform Based on Rapid PolyJet 3D Printing Fabrication Toward Biomedical Analysis Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 3rd International Symposium on Material and Electrical Engineering Conference (ISMEE)
abstract: Limited manufacturing technology and upscaling potential are the main obstacles in bringing microfluidic devices into real-life applications. This study presents a combinative approach using 3D printing and printed circuit board (PCB) technologies to solve the problem. A lab-on-printed circuit board (LoPCB) microfluidic device with the ability to generate microdroplets was successfully designed and fabricated to confirm the performance of the proposed rapid fabrication method. The device’s operation was investigated. The proposed rapid prototyping does not require a cleanroom as in general approaches for microfluidic fabrication. The experimental results of microdroplet generation and impedance fluidic flow detection on fabricated devices have proved that the combination of 3D printing and PCB technologies was simple and easy. The use of polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS), a bio-compatible material, enables the application of bio- component sensing using the electrical approach by the proposed fabrication technique. It is highly feasible to apply in microfluidic devices aiming for compact lab-on-a-chip (LoC) systems in biomedical analysis applications.

articleTitle: A Study on Hybrid Renewable Electric Systems in Northern Province, Sri Lanka
publicationTitle: 2021 3rd International Symposium on Material and Electrical Engineering Conference (ISMEE)
abstract: Solar and wind energy-based renewable energy systems are environmentally friendly alternatives to fossil-fuel-based conventional power plants for meeting rising energy demand. Because of the uncertainties and intermittency of a single energy source, a properly designed hybrid system combining wind and Solar can effectively increase the system’s reliability. The Northern Province of Sri Lanka, where solar and wind potentials are significantly higher than the rest of the country, is experiencing an increase in electrical power demand. This paper aims to design and analyze a hybrid electrical power plant that combines solar and wind energy for use in Northern Province to meet future energy demands. Each province district's wind and solar potential are analyzed to determine the best location for the design to be implemented. Regression analysis is used to forecast future energy demand based on historical demand data. During the design stage, mathematical equations determine the rating and number of components. The results show that the Kilinochchi district in Northern Province is the best location for installing the system. Also, results show that the proposed 250 MW hybrid system can effectively address Northern Province’s growing energy demand. The greenhouse emissions of an average of 739.521 million kg per year can be reduced.

articleTitle: Digital De-cluttering To Manage Necessary Information for Young Generation
publicationTitle: 2021 3rd International Symposium on Material and Electrical Engineering Conference (ISMEE)
abstract: This research aims to analyze a digital minimalist lifestyle to manage necessary information through digital de-cluttering for sustainable young generation life. The research method used is a qualitative approach with a virtual ethnographic type. The data is collected by observing the content in videos of the YouTube channel "Satu Persen" through the comments column and conducting online interviews with subscribers as additional information. The data analysis in this research used virtual ethnography and the data is validated by source triangulation. The research result finds that the content of the YouTube channel "Satu Persen" educates a digital minimalist lifestyle concept by reducing digital content or applications to maintain mental health from detoxifying information and manage well necessary information. This research also recommends a Digital De- cluttering of Digital Minimalist Lifestyle Model which could be applied to the young generation in carrying out a minimalist lifestyle.

articleTitle: Review on Manufacturing Methods of Functionally Graded Material of Solid-State Batteries
publicationTitle: 2021 3rd International Symposium on Material and Electrical Engineering Conference (ISMEE)
abstract: Lithium-Ion Battery (LIB) has been a critical component for solar Photovoltaic and wind energy implementation, Electric Vehicle (EV) implementation, and other electronic devices that require a battery. However, further LIB development exposed safety issues such as battery explosion due to short circuits caused by lithium dendrite growth. All- Solid-State Battery (SSB) is considered the most promising prospect due to the non-flammable characteristic of the SSB. Nevertheless, some problems still need to be solved, for example, impedance resulting from interfacial and internal resistance of both electrodes and electrolytes, ionic conductivity, and battery’s mechanical properties. Therefore, several studies show that Functionally Graded Materials (FGM) implemented for SSB electrolytes and electrodes is one of the prospects to solve this problem. This review paper discusses recent research on SSB and FGM, manufacturing methods, and future development of FGM manufacturing for SSB.

articleTitle: Mathematical Modeling of the Energy Conversion System for DFIG Based Wind Turbines
publicationTitle: 2021 3rd International Symposium on Material and Electrical Engineering Conference (ISMEE)
abstract: In this paper, we study the control, operation and stability characteristics of Doubly-Fed Induction Generators Based Wind Turbines. In existent transmission grids, the inverter based design has proven to be the most reliable and efficient topology due to its higher ability to supply reactive during faults at the point of interconnection to keep the wind farms online. Nevertheless, there still exists limits and is also dependent on the design of the grid that the turbines are being integrated in. The mathematical model of the energy conversion system of the wind farm is crucial to the system planners to fully capture the behavior of the wind farm over its operation. As such, mathematically modeling the system and control mechanism provides a means to better understand the system by translating it graphically into vector reference frames. This paper attempts to address the modeling of the energy conversion system of a DFIG-based wind farm. The models can be beneficial to the designers and planners to optimally design and operate the wind turbine.
